text:
The channel opens on an officer in an unmarked pressure suit. Your transponder record and a damage report are open side by side.

"You hit $entity.catchrelease_harpoonHitmanVictim with $entity.catchrelease_harpoonHitmanOffence in $entity.catchrelease_harpoonHitmanOrigin. Recovery logged your transponder code."

"Probably shouldn't have done that."

The officer closes the report.

"We're here to settle the account."

The channel opens on an officer in an unmarked pressure suit. Your transponder record and a damage report are open side by side.

"You hit $entity.catchrelease_harpoonHitmanVictim with $entity.catchrelease_harpoonHitmanOffence in $entity.catchrelease_harpoonHitmanOrigin. Recovery logged your transponder code."

The officer closes the report.

"Client's gone, but the escrow cleared before they got done in."

"We're here to settle the account."

The officer glances at the contract.

"Cancellation is permitted provided the damages and legal fees are settled in full, immediately. $entity.catchrelease_harpoonHitmanBribeDGS credits."

The transfer clears. The officer closes your file.

"Contract cancelled. Try not to harpoon someone important, next time."

The channel opens on a busy damage-control compartment. Someone reads your transponder code. Someone else asks whether the object recovered from their hull belongs to you. Your comms officer confirms that it does. There is a short silence. "Fishing gear." The speaker looks off-screen. "You fired fishing gear at our ship."

"Hegemony Navy." $PersonRank $personName reads from the incident form. "Hull damage. Unregistered heavy projectile. Recovery of an unidentified ROD assembly from the impact site." A second slate is passed into frame. "Naval Intelligence gets the hardware. You get the report."

"Damage assessment is complete." $PersonRank $personName is already looking at the invoice. "Repair labor, lost operating time, forensic recovery and disposal of your projectile." A brief glance up. "We retained the projectile."
$PersonRank $personName looks at the damage feed. Then at you. "Whatever purpose that machine was built for, captain, this was not it."

The speaker has the recovered ROD head on the table behind them.

"Accident?" They jab a finger toward it. "You cast Moloch's iron through a ship full of Ludd's children and call it an accident?"

Someone off-screen shouts assent.

"Fire another. See what answer you get."
$personName turns the recovered projectile toward the camera. "You hooked us." A grin appears despite everything. "Actually hooked us." The grin goes away. "Don't do it twice."

"You discharged an unregistered heavy device at a vessel of the Sindrian Diktat." $PersonRank $personName checks the record. "I am required to ask whether the act was deliberate." The slate is set aside. "I have spared us both the formality."

$PersonRank $personName has several regulations open. "I have weapon discharge, negligent recovery operations and collision damage." Another document opens. "I do not have 'industrial harpoon'." They sigh. "I will improvise."
"You put a hole in us with fishing gear." $personName rubs the bridge of $hisOrHer nose. "I have to explain that sentence to a yardmaster."

text:
"We have a damage report naming your ship."

$PersonRank $personName checks the attached image.

"The object in question is described as fishing equipment."

A second look.

"Heavy fishing equipment."

"The settlement is $entity.catchrelease_harpoonFineDGS credits. Pay it here and the incident closes as negligent discharge."

"Hegemony Navy. Heave to."

$PersonRank $personName reads the charge.

"Unregistered heavy projectile, damage to a registered hull and reckless discharge within a patrolled volume."

"$entity.catchrelease_harpoonFineDGS credits."

A slate is set aside.

"Pay it and this remains an accident report."

"You've damaged Tri-Tachyon property. A fine for the damage and associated recovery costs has been assessed."

The figure is already on-screen.

"Hull repair, lost schedule time and recovery of foreign hardware: $entity.catchrelease_harpoonFineDGS credits."

"Peace be with you. Cut your drive."

$PersonRank $personName looks at the damage report.

"You damaged a crewed vessel with equipment no prudent captain should point at one."

"The repair is $entity.catchrelease_harpoonFineDGS credits."

"Pay the people whose hull you opened."

"You put Moloch's iron through a ship full of people and now you want this treated as an accident?"

The claim figure appears.

"$entity.catchrelease_harpoonFineDGS credits. Pay it."

A finger jabs at the recovered-hardware image.

"Then throw that thing out an airlock."

"Hold up."

$PersonName grins.

"Word says you put a fishing harpoon through somebody's plating."

The grin broadens.

"Very funny story. Expensive story."

"$entity.catchrelease_harpoonFineDGS and we're even."

"You discharged an unregistered heavy device into a registered vessel under Sindrian protection."

"The State is prepared to dispose of this as an administrative penalty: $entity.catchrelease_harpoonFineDGS credits."

$PersonRank $personName folds $hisOrHer hands, then looks back to you.

"You will not be offered this courtesy twice."

$PersonRank $personName has assembled several statutes into a workable stack.

"League regulations authorize a fine of $entity.catchrelease_harpoonFineDGS credits for damage to associated hulls by... heavy salvaging equipment. Yeah."

"If you dislike my interpretation, the appeals committee meets quarterly."

"Ease off."

$personName looks at a damage report.

"Somebody you hooked filed a claim. Filing a claim means I get to fly out here and say $entity.catchrelease_harpoonFineDGS credits."

"Pay it and both of us get our day back."

text:
The provisioner looks up from a spread of manifests as your connection opens.

"Captain. Good timing."

A supplier line is pulled to the front of the slate, your comm ID already attached to it.

"Let's see where the order stands."
A local provisioner has three delivery manifests open beside a supplier list. The outbound section has more orders than names.

options: catchrelease_standingOrder_ask:Talk to the provisioner with the delivery manifests

text:
"You're supplying catch? Good. I've got kitchens buying faster than my regulars are landing."

The provisioner turns the open order toward you.

"$catchreleaseAskCap. Meet the line as written."

"$catchreleaseDaysCap. $catchreleaseRewardCap on delivery."

"Good."

Your comm ID goes into the next empty line.
The provisioner closes the entry and opens the next name on the supplier list.
"$catchreleaseAskCap. Same order, $catchreleaseDaysLeft left."

The provisioner checks the containers against the manifest and closes the order.

The agreed payment is transferred to your account.

The head chef answers from the edge of a roaring kitchen, wipes one hand on an apron and props a slate against a stack of ingredient cards.

"Captain. Thank the gods."

$HeOrShe glances back toward the kitchen.

"All right. Tell me you've got something useful."
A cook in stained whites has three ingredient cards laid out beneath the name of one dish. Two supplier names have been crossed out hard enough to score the slate.

options: catchrelease_chef_ask:Talk to the cook with the ingredient cards

text:
"I'm putting $catchreleaseDish on the menu. Apparently half the station has decided they can't live without it. It needs three different catches."

The chef taps each card in turn.

"$catchreleaseAsk. Yes, all of it. I know. Take it up with my customers."

"$catchreleaseDaysCap. After that I either have the fish or I have a dining room full of people asking why I don't. $catchreleaseRewardCap when the full order reaches my kitchen."
"Good. Leave the handling tags on. Last thing I need is the prep crew arguing over which one goes where."
The chef removes your name from the supplier list, then stares at the three ingredient cards as though one of them has personally offended $himOrHer.

"$catchreleaseAskCap. All three. $catchreleaseDaysLeft left."

"$PlayerSirOrMadam, I have every table booked for this. Please don't make me invent a new menu before service."

The chef checks each handling tag against the ingredient cards, then starts passing containers to the prep crew.

"Yes. Good. That's all of them."

$HeOrShe turns toward the kitchen.

"Move! I've got the fish, you've got no excuses!"

The agreed transfer clears. The transmission cuts while $heOrShe is still shouting instructions down the line.

The young factor accepts the connection with the current order already open. It appears as a solid line among several dotted forecasts.

"Captain. Good. I've been updating the model from the committed volume."

$HeOrShe brings your order to the center of the display.

"Where are we?"
A young factor in an expensive jacket has a ten-page business case open on $hisOrHer slate. A half-finished drink sits at one corner of the table.

options: catchrelease_startup_ask:Hear the pitch from the young factor in the expensive jacket

text:
"You fish. Good. That's the difficult side."

$HeOrShe closes three projections and opens another, packed with margins and rising curves.

"I have ten pages proving people buy fresh catch. What I don't have is one supplier line I can point at and say, there, that works."

$HeOrShe taps the first empty figure in the model.

"You give me that, I can build from something real."

"Restaurant kitchens already buy fresh catch, and between the private clubs and conservatories I have enough projected demand to fill several pages."

$HeOrShe flicks through sales projections tied to population and prevailing catch prices.

"The demand case is finished. What I need now is a shipment I can put on the other side of it."

$HeOrShe opens a flow diagram running from your delivery to a projected customer handoff. Every stage has a margin and turnaround estimate. The operator fields are blank.

"That's downstream execution."

You indicate the empty fields.

"Of course they're empty. There isn't any volume yet."

$HeOrShe enlarges the first stage instead.

"Once you prove the catch is coming in, I have something to negotiate around. The rest is capacity, and capacity is purchasable."

$HeOrShe taps your end of the flow.

"First, I need the part that isn't a projection."

"If this one closes, we raise the volume."

The agreed transfer clears. $HeOrShe folds the signed receipt into the model, replacing one of the projected figures with an actual one.

"Now I can price growth against something that exists."

$HeOrShe sends the next order.

A much larger forecast opens behind them. You immediately notice the lack of confirmed customers.

"That changes the financing case considerably."

$HeOrShe sends the next order.

The agreed transfer clears. $HeOrShe reads the final delivery receipt twice.

The three receipts take up half a page in the business case. A distribution network spreads across the rest in pale forecast lines.

"Three completed runs. That's the supply chain proven."

$HeOrShe is already revising the demand projections.

The $manOrWoman answers promptly. A household schedule remains open on $hisOrHer slate, with your name brought discreetly to the top.

"Captain. Good day."

$HeOrShe sets the slate aside.

"You wished to speak about the little matter of the fish."
A $manOrWoman in an immaculately cut coat sits beside an untouched drink. The chair opposite has been placed a little farther from the table than would be strictly necessary.

text:
The $manOrWoman rises before you reach the table and indicates it.

"Captain. How good of you to come. I make certain purchases on behalf of a private household. I am given to understand that you procure live specimens."

$HeOrShe waits for you to sit. $HeOrShe remains standing.

"We find ourselves in want of one."

The chief butler of the household."

"I attend to his rooms and appointments. He has entrusted the matter to me."

"Display."

$HeOrShe turns a slate sufficiently for you to see it, though does not pass it across. It shows a tank built neatly into the wall of an office.

"For his receiving room. The space has already been measured. It will not be going anywhere near the kitchens, I assure you."

$HeOrShe adjusts the slate by a fraction.

"One specimen. $catchreleaseAsk."

A pause.

"That is a minimum, captain. Something with a little presence is wanted. Species is immaterial, as is culinary merit."

"The household will pay $catchreleaseReward upon delivery."

"Very good."

$HeOrShe makes a small notation on the slate.

"Return it here when convenient. There is no need to trouble the household with a delivery."

Your mission log updates.

"I see."

$HeOrShe removes your name from the schedule with no visible disappointment.

"I shall place the matter back with the usual suppliers."

"One specimen. $catchreleaseAskCap."

$HeOrShe consults the original note.

"Here, if you please. The household needn't be involved."

A dock porter places the container on the scale. The $manOrWoman watches the reading from $hisOrHer slate, then gives the specimen itself a brief, appraising look.

"Yes."

Another glance at the weight.

"That will do very nicely."

The agreed payment changes hands.

"Thank you, captain. I shall see that it finds its proper place."

By the time the porter takes the container away, the $manOrWoman has already moved on to the next item in $hisOrHer schedule.

The curator accepts the connection from beside a row of open accession entries.

$HeOrShe turns an accession list toward you.

"We're missing $catchreleaseAskCap."

"Fine-grade specimens can go on display, low-coherence specimens go into the comparative record. Either works for me."

"$catchreleaseDaysCap. $catchreleaseRewardCap on successful recovery."

$HeOrShe matches each seal to an entry before the first container is moved to the collection transport.

"Good. That's enough for the exhibition."

"We're having a tournament."

The quiet child points to two empty spaces near the bottom.

"But we need two more fish."
"And he won't let me pick."
"Because you always pick yours first."

The loud child looks at you.

"One fish each. No swapping. Don't mess with the other person's fish."

The quiet child adds something to the list.

"Because he says I always take the better one," says the loud child.

"You do."

"Not always."

"Almost always."

The loud child points at you.

"$heOrShe doesn't care which one I get."

The quiet child considers this, then nods.

"Yeah."

text: The Last Entry
Holding for catalogue filing

Expedition $entity.catchreleaseFleetExpedition has completed its survey, but one specimen entry remains open. $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName needs the requested specimen to close the entry and file the catalogue without voiding the expedition's survey classification.
The expedition will accept delivery on the following terms.
"Survey vessel $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName, registry $entity.catchreleaseFleetRegistry, expedition $entity.catchreleaseFleetExpedition."

"Expedition $entity.catchreleaseFleetExpedition has finished its survey. Telemetry is in. Every accession record but one is closed."

They bring up the open entry.

"If I file the catalogue incomplete, it voids the expedition's survey classification. So I'm holding it open. Berth and specimen-holding fees keep running while I do."

"We need $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk. Compensation is $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestReward. I can hold the filing for $entity.catchreleaseFleetDays."

"Good. I'll transmit the catalogue entry and the relevant range references now."

The files arrive under expedition $entity.catchreleaseFleetExpedition.

"Understood. No commitment recorded."

They send the same catalogue entry and range references.

"If you bring us a qualifying specimen before the filing window closes, we'll take it."

"Understood. We'll keep the entry open and continue looking."

The officer closes the channel.

"Survey vessel $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName, registry $entity.catchreleaseFleetRegistry. Catalogue is still open. Berth and specimen-holding fees are still running."

"We still need $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk."

The expedition staff take custody of the specimen. It goes first to the scale, then beneath a fixed imaging rig while the data officer checks the accession number against the open catalogue entry.

"Measurements accepted. Photographs attached."

They enter the final field and close the record.

"Catalogue filed."

The officer opens the original sighting entry.

"Entry date $entity.catchreleaseFleetEntryDate. Coordinates $entity.catchreleaseFleetCoordinates. Signature $entity.catchreleaseFleetSignature."

They check the name against the personnel index.

"No crew member by that name has ever served aboard $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName."

They close the personnel index.

"We still need the specimen to close the entry."

"That's the complete catalogue filed."

The officer checks the submission receipt, then returns to the original sighting record.

"We'll retain the original entry with the expedition archive."

"Good work, captain. $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName out."
The Escrow
Closing out the contract

Recovery vessel $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName is trying to close contract $entity.catchreleaseFleetContract. The original specimen disappeared with its carrier, but the contract allows a replacement. The skipper needs $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk before the outstanding liability grows any further.
The skipper offers the following terms for a replacement.
"Recovery vessel $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName. Skipper speaking. I've got a contract I need off my books.

"$entity.catchreleaseFleetContract. Somebody sold a specimen two cycles ago. Carrier vanished before delivery, cargo and all. We got handed the recovery."

They scroll through several pages of figures.

"We're liable for $entity.catchreleaseFleetLiability at the moment. That number keeps going up until somebody closes the delivery."

"Doesn't have to be the original specimen. There's a replacement clause."

The skipper brings up the specification.

"$entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk will satisfy it. I'll pay $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestReward if you can get one here inside $entity.catchreleaseFleetDays."

"All right. I'll put you down as an outside supplier."

"We still need $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk. It must be caught in $entity.catchreleaseFleetSystem under this subcontract."

The prospecting crew photographs the specimen beside the capture record. The contract officer verifies the timestamp and $entity.catchreleaseFleetSystem coordinates, then appends both to claim file $entity.catchreleaseFleetCharter.

The updated file is transmitted before the specimen is moved to storage.

The officer opens the loss entry.

"Field equipment failure. Write-off: $entity.catchreleaseFleetWriteoff. Personnel unharmed."

They close the entry.

"We've moved the requirement to vendor supply."

"Claim file $entity.catchreleaseFleetCharter has cleared review. Our exclusive survey rights in $entity.catchreleaseFleetSystem are renewed."

The unaffiliated survey ship leaves the jump point shortly after the renewal posts.

"That closes the exposure. $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName out."

"We're not naming them. They are unaffiliated and have not breached our survey rights."

The officer opens the traffic record.

"Recorded loiter time: $entity.catchreleaseFleetCompetitorLoiter. Estimated fuel endurance: $entity.catchreleaseFleetCompetitorEndurance."

"They can afford to wait."

A Tri-Tachyon survey formation is holding position in $entity.catchreleaseFleetSystem while an unaffiliated survey ship waits at the jump point. A priority commercial request is being broadcast on open channels.
The Mandate
Closing the expedition mandate

Science expedition $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName needs $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk to close the final deliverable under mandate $entity.catchreleaseFleetMandate. The convoy must depart within $entity.catchreleaseFleetDays when its escort fuel window closes.
The expedition's contingency request is recorded on the following terms.
"Science expedition $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName, operating under mandate $entity.catchreleaseFleetMandate. We could use your help."

"I've spent years on this expedition. Mandate $entity.catchreleaseFleetMandate has one deliverables line left open: a specimen with abyssal provenance."

"Our retrieval rig was lost at the site. The escort's fuel window is fixed, and an incomplete mandate will not renew."

They check the departure schedule.

"We need $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk. Contingency allocation is $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestReward. We have $entity.catchreleaseFleetDays."

"Good. I'll transmit the mandate extract and provenance requirements."

The files arrive from $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName.

"Understood. No commitment entered."

The principal investigator transmits the same mandate extract and provenance requirements.

"If you obtain a qualifying specimen before departure, hail $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName."

"Understood. We'll keep the deliverable open while the fuel window allows."

"$entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName out."

"When we first spoke, the fuel margin was a departure date. Now it's a departure time."

"We have $entity.catchreleaseFleetDays. We still need $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk."

The principal investigator checks the specimen's provenance against the expedition telemetry, then signs the final deliverables line under mandate $entity.catchreleaseFleetMandate.

The completed mandate file is transmitted to the member-state review office.

They hand you a worn physical folder containing the surviving drawings from the lost rig.

The principal investigator opens the equipment-loss report.

"Deployment nominal at $entity.catchreleaseFleetDeploymentDepth. Last telemetry ended $entity.catchreleaseFleetTelemetryEnd. No recovery attempt remained inside the $entity.catchreleaseFleetSafetyMargin safety margin."

They close the report.

"The rig was written off."

"Mandate $entity.catchreleaseFleetMandate is complete. The convoy can make its fuel window, and renewal can proceed."

The escort begins forming the return order.

"I'm going to sleep through part of the trip home."

"$entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName out."
A Persean League member-state science convoy is inbound from the deep fringe and holding at the edge of the system. $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName is broadcasting an urgent research request.
The Parley Fish
Waiting on the parley

Pirate fleet $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName is disputing who gets to collect protection money around $entity.catchreleaseFleetRupture. Their captain wants $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk caught there after the job is accepted and brought back within $entity.catchreleaseFleetDays. Anything caught earlier is no good.
The captain offers the following terms.
"Pirate fleet $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName. You got a fishing rig that works?"

The captain has a scratched-up chart of $entity.catchreleaseFleetRupture open when the link comes through.

"We collect off crews working this rupture. Another pack of bastards decided they'd rather collect it themselves."

"We traded a little fire. Nobody lost a ship, so somebody had the bright idea to talk before that changes."

They tap the rupture on the chart.

"There's an old rule for this. You claim the water, you bring something fresh out of it to the table. Shows you're actually working the place and not just sitting on it with guns."

"Has to be caught after I stamp the job. Don't bring me something that's been rolling around your hold since Corvus."

"I need $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk from $entity.catchreleaseFleetRupture. Pay is $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestReward. You've got $entity.catchreleaseFleetDays."

"Good. Sending the fix now."

The location and job record arrive from $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName.

"There's a timestamp on it. Anything caught before that stays yours."

"Fine. I'm not putting your name on anything yet."

The captain sends over the location and job record.

"If you pull $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk out of $entity.catchreleaseFleetRupture before the meeting, hail us."

"Suit yourself. We'll find something else to put on the table."

"$entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName out."

"Other crew's still across the rupture. Every time one of ours gets close they light their drives and act like they're about to do something."

"We've got $entity.catchreleaseFleetDays. I still need $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk out of $entity.catchreleaseFleetRupture."

A deckhand hauls a battered cold-case onto the bridge. The captain checks your catch against the job record.

"$entity.catchreleaseFleetRupture. Timestamp $entity.catchreleaseFleetCatchTimestamp. Good."

The deckhand closes the case and runs a fresh seal over a latch already scarred by several older ones.

"Nobody opens that until we're sitting across from the other lot."

"Then we do it the expensive way."

The captain brings up rough strength estimates for the two fleets.

"We can take them. Lose a couple hulls doing it, maybe more. Then we spend a month welding ships back together while nobody pays us a credit for working $entity.catchreleaseFleetRupture."

They shut the display.

"I'd rather buy a fish."

"Parley held. Other lot took the terms and everybody left with the same number of ships they came in with."

The captain clears the engagement marks from the plot.

"We're square, captain."

"Protection money, tolls, licensing. Call it what you want."

The captain points at $entity.catchreleaseFleetRupture.

"Crews work our water, they pay. We keep the next pack of guns from taking it off them. That's the arrangement."

"Still need the fish."
A pirate combat formation is hanging around $entity.catchreleaseFleetRupture. Someone on the open trade band is asking for a fishing crew.
Stranded Fleet
Making emergency repairs

A stranded ship has an intermittent drive and a ration printer that can no longer process its normal feedstock. Engineering only has the parts and crew to repair one of them. The printer can take fresh catch directly, so the engineer needs $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk from this system or an adjacent one within $entity.catchreleaseFleetDays.
The engineer's request is recorded on the following terms.
"Engineering officer aboard $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName. Our drive is failing and we've got another problem besides. If you've got a moment, we could use some support."

The engineers face shows deep, dark bags beneath $hisOrHer eyes, testament to the rather severe predicament $heOrShe appears to be in.

"Our drive keeps dropping out. That's where my repair crew ought to be, but they are stuck fixing a ludd-darned rations printer."

They bring up a fault report.

"Ration printer won't take our normal feedstock. I had to pull people off fixing the drive because I'd rather be stuck than starving, but it's not sustainable."

The engineer opens the printer manual.

"There is a bypass. It'll take fresh catch directly. Domain feedstock table, commodity code $entity.catchreleaseFleetFeedstockCode."

They turn the relevant entry toward the pickup.

"It has to be fresh enough for the intake, so this system or one adjacent. Bring us $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk and I can leave the printer alone and keep working on the drive."

"We can pay $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestReward. We have $entity.catchreleaseFleetDays."

"Good. I'll send you the feedstock entry and receiving instructions."

The files arrive over the comm link.

"Understood. No commitment."

The engineer transmits the same feedstock entry and receiving instructions.

"If you find $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk before the window closes, hail us."

"Understood. We'll keep working on the drive."

The channel closes.

"Printer's still down. We're into reserve rations now, and every watch has sent somebody down to ask about it."

"We still need $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk. We have $entity.catchreleaseFleetDays."

The catch goes directly into the ration printer's feedstock intake. The engineer checks the commodity code, closes the access panel, and starts the processing cycle.

The fault indicator clears. A few seconds later, the machinery starts up.

The engineer opens the feedstock table.

"Code $entity.catchreleaseFleetFeedstockCode. Fresh catch."

They scroll through the surrounding entries.

"Rendered protein stock above it. Agricultural slurry below."

The engineer closes the manual.

"The printer doesn't care much where the protein came from."

"Printer's running. That's food taken care of."

The engineer brings the drive repair schedule back onto the slate.

"Now I can keep everyone on the drive."

"The printer can turn one fish into weeks of ration stock."

The engineer checks the figures again.

"We cook it ourselves, we get dinner. I'd rather have the weeks."
A ship is broadcasting a standard distress call. Its drive plume flickers in and out as it struggles to hold position.
Fleet on a Hunt
Searching
A local captain has spent eleven weeks searching for $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk and is offering his entire haul in exchange. He needs the specimen within $entity.catchreleaseFleetDays.
The captain's offer is recorded on the following terms.
"Captain here. If you've got a minute, I'd like to talk."

The captain looks tired enough that eleven weeks sounds plausible before he says it.

"We've been hunting one fish for eleven weeks. Wrong equipment for the job, but it's what we had."

"I need $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk. Nothing else will do."

He brings up the cargo transfer.

"You bring it here, you take $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestReward. That's the whole haul. This trip was never supposed to make money."

"I have $entity.catchreleaseFleetDays left."

"Good. I'll send you the record for $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk."

The file arrives over the comm link.

"Bring it here when you have it."

"Fine. No promise."

He transmits the same record.

"If you find $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk before the window closes, hail me."

"Understood."

The captain closes the channel.

"Any luck with $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk?"

"I have $entity.catchreleaseFleetDays left."

The captain takes the container and inspects the specimen longer than a buyer would. No specification sheet comes out.

He turns it once, checks one side, then the other.

"That's it."

A cargo order goes out. His crew begins transferring the haul to your ship.

"I was keeping a collection for my old captain."

"I got into debt and sold one piece of it. My decision. Wasn't my property."

"He's retiring, and the collection gets inspected before it changes hands."

"Eleven weeks. That's the part you need."

"Eleven weeks with the wrong gear, and you brought it back in one trip."

He looks at the container again.

"That's all I needed."
Short of Quota
Filling quota

Fishing fleet $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName is short $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk on station provisioning contract $entity.catchreleaseFleetContract. The purser is trying to make up the shortfall before the $entity.catchreleaseFleetFilingDate filing, which is due in $entity.catchreleaseFleetDays.
The purser can authorize a supplemental purchase on the following terms.
"Fishing fleet $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName, purser's office. Sorry to trouble you, captain. We're short on a provisioning contract and I understand you've got fishing gear aboard."

The purser comes on from the working deck with a ledger slate tucked beneath $hisOrHer arm. Someone calls a tally in the background; $heOrShe waits for it, enters the figure, then looks back to the pickup.

"We're short $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk on contract $entity.catchreleaseFleetContract. I've had the hold counted three times. That's the number."

$HeOrShe brings up the filing schedule.

"The return goes in on $entity.catchreleaseFleetFilingDate. If I send it short, the station can kick the contract into arbitration. They may leave the rate alone. They may decide the whole schedule needs reviewing. I would very much prefer not to give them the opportunity."

The purser opens another ledger and spends a moment comparing the two.

"I don't have authority to amend the quota, but I can buy against the shortfall. I can authorize $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestReward from this season's margin without sending it upstairs for approval."

"If you can bring us $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk within $entity.catchreleaseFleetDays, I can still file the contract complete."

"Thank you. I'll record you as an outside supplier and send the relevant contract line."

The contract extract and grade record arrive from $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName.

"Please use that grade schedule when you sort the catch. If anything falls outside it, I can't put it against the quota."

"Of course. I won't record an obligation."

The purser sends over the contract line and grade record.

"If you can make up the shortfall before $entity.catchreleaseFleetFilingDate, hail us. I'll keep the purchase authorization open."

"Yes, understood. Sorry to take your time."

The purser glances down at the ledger again.

"We'll keep our boats out and see what comes in."

"$entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName out."

The purser has the quota ledger open before the channel finishes connecting.

"We're still short $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk. A boat came in last watch and I thought we'd made some of it back, but most of the catch graded below contract."

$HeOrShe checks the filing schedule again.

"$entity.catchreleaseFleetFilingDate. $entity.catchreleaseFleetDays left. I'm keeping the purchase authorization open as long as I can."

The purser meets the transfer on the working deck with two tally clerks and the contract grade sheet.

The catch is counted and checked as it comes across. One specimen is set aside, examined again, then returned to the accepted lot.

The purser watches the running total until the last container is entered.

"There. That's the quota."

$HeOrShe checks the figure once more before signing the receipt.

The purser brings up the catch records from earlier in the season.

"We planned against the same grounds we've used for years. Some stopped producing, some shifted far enough that we're burning more fuel finding them than the contract allows for."

$HeOrShe scrolls back through several older returns.

"On paper we're supposed to be able to make this quota with the boats and gear we have. Every previous season says so, which is exactly what the station will point to if I file short."

The purser closes the older records.

"I can't change that before filing. I can only try to make up what's missing."

The purser is still looking at the completed tally.

"Yes. That balances."

A long breath escapes $himOrHer as the filing status is updated.

"I can send the return in complete now. Payment's authorized, captain. Thank you."
Hungry Fleet
Rationing

The crew of $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName has spent $entity.catchreleaseFleetRationDays days on printed protein, and galley morale is failing. Their cook needs $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk within $entity.catchreleaseFleetDays to put fresh food back on the menu.
The galley chief's provisioning offer is recorded on the following terms.
"Galley chief aboard $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName. I'm the cook, and command has wisely left this negotiation to me."

The galley chief comes on from the mess.

"We've been on printed protein for $entity.catchreleaseFleetRationDays days. Nutritionally adequate, and thoroughly humiliating."

"The crew gave command a signed petition this morning. No demands, just a proposed menu, itemized by watch."

$heOrShe holds the petition at an arms length as if personally offended by the implication.

"Command decided nobody trusts them to negotiate dinner anymore, so here I am."

"We need $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk. I can authorize $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestReward. We have $entity.catchreleaseFleetDays."

"Good. I'll send the order and receiving instructions."

The files arrive from $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName.

"Understood. No commitment."

The galley chief transmits the same order and receiving instructions.

"If you can fill it before the window closes, hail us."

"Understood. I'll keep looking."

"$entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName out."

"We're at $entity.catchreleaseFleetRationDays days on printed protein."

The galley chief holds up the petition.

"It has an appendix now."

"We still need $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk. We have $entity.catchreleaseFleetDays."

The galley chief inspects the delivery container by container, checking each specimen before waving it through to prep.

Their shoulders finally come down.

"Good. Cold storage, second rack. Knives out. Somebody get the large pans hot."

The galley erupts into motion.

"Nutrition is acceptable."

The galley chief looks back into the mess.

"Last meal, thirty people sat through the entire watch change chewing in silence and looking at the printer."

They turn back to you.

"Morale is not acceptable."

"The galley has stopped threatening mutiny."

The chief reads from the crew's proposed menu.

"Roasted catch, proper stock, fresh portions for night watch."

They fold the petition.

"That's your thank-you."

id: # fleet quest: scavenger with a dead engine

text: Scavenger with a Dead Engine
Repacking the drive coil

The scavenger $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName needs $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk to produce substitute packing gel for a failing drive coil. Catch from the current system or an adjacent one will qualify if delivered within $entity.catchreleaseFleetDays.
The repair supply request is recorded on the following terms.
"Coil technician aboard the scavenger $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName. We've got a drive repair held up for lack of one consumable."

The technician his fiddling with the drive diagnostics.

"One of our drive coils is failing. We can save it if we repack the winding before the insulation goes."

"What we don't have is packing gel. Yard manual section $entity.catchreleaseFleetManualSection lists an approved substitute compound rendered from fresh local catch. Apparently."

They tap the relevant line.

"Catch from this system or an adjacent one is acceptable. We need $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk. We can pay $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestReward out of the salvage haul. We have $entity.catchreleaseFleetDays."

"Good. I'll send the manual extract and receiving instructions."

The files arrive from $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName.

"Understood. No commitment."

The technician transmits the same manual extract and receiving instructions.

"If you find what we need before the window closes, hail us."

"Understood. We'll keep looking for another supply."

"$entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName out."

"Coil condition is $entity.catchreleaseFleetCoilCondition. It was better yesterday."

"We still need $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk. We have $entity.catchreleaseFleetDays."

The specimen is transferred to engineering.

Some time later, the repaired drive comes up to a steady tone. Conversation on the working deck stops for a few seconds while the crew listens.

A deckhand starts the salvage invoice, reaches the description field, and leaves the cursor blinking.

The technician opens $entity.catchreleaseFleetManualSection again.

"Rendered fraction, eighteen to twenty-two percent by mass. Stable from minus forty to two hundred ten Celsius."

They continue down the procedure.

"Render, filter, bring to working temperature, pack the winding voids, then cycle the coil twice under low load."

The manual closes.

"I didn't write it."

"The gel packed cleanly. Coil is holding."

The technician glances at the open copy of $entity.catchreleaseFleetManualSection.

"Manual was right."
A scavenger vessel is holding position with its drive cold. A standard assistance request is running on the local trade band.
Collector's Commission
Waiting

A private collector aboard $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName needs $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk after repeated brokered purchases were reassigned before transfer. They are commissioning a direct catch to bypass the market and require delivery within $entity.catchreleaseFleetDays.
The private commission is recorded on the following terms.
"Private vessel $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName. I have a collection commission to place, if you are taking work."

"I have spent two years trying to acquire $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk. Three brokers accepted deposits, returned them, and reassigned each specimen before transfer."

"I suspect another collector is bidding through agents. A direct catch keeps the transaction out of that market, and thus, free from interference."

"Price is no issue. I am offering $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestReward. I need delivery within $entity.catchreleaseFleetDays."

"Very good. I will transmit the collection entry and receiving requirements."

The files arrive from $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName.

"Understood. I will record no commitment."

The collector transmits the same collection entry and receiving requirements.

"If you obtain $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk within the window, hail $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName."

"Understood. I will continue the search."

"$entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName out."

"The tank is still running. I checked the water chemistry this morning; it remains within the holding profile."

"I still require $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk. There are $entity.catchreleaseFleetDays remaining."

The collector receives the container personally and takes it to the display tank.

They compare the holding temperatures, set the acclimation flow, and wait beside the tank until the transfer is complete.

The specimen settles behind the glass beneath the engraved nameplate.

"Carthen & Vale, Morrow Exchange, and Silex Acquisitions. Dates: $entity.catchreleaseFleetBrokerDates."

The collector opens the three transaction records.

"Each accepted my deposit. Each returned it when the specimen was reallocated immediately before transfer. The records suggest the same outside buyer acting through agents."

They close the files.

"I have had enough of being sniped."

"Two years of refusals, and there it is."

The collector checks the tank once more.

"Whoever was buying all of these can keep them. Mine is the best."

The collector turns the pickup toward a display tank. It is empty, lit, and filtered; an engraved nameplate is fixed beneath the glass.

"Eighteen point five Celsius. Ten-hour display cycle."

They turn the pickup back.
Settling a Bet
Arguing

Two watches aboard $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName disagree about what they found at the same fishing ground. There's money riding on it now, and the captain has asked for $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk to settle the matter within $entity.catchreleaseFleetDays.
The wager has the following terms.

"Scavenger fleet $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName. Captain speaking. I've got an argument between two watches that's gone on long enough. They put money on it, naturally. If you fish, you might be able to settle it for us."

The captain sends over two survey logs from the same fishing ground.

"First watch says these returns are the species we're after. Second watch says they could be anything, and that the first lot got lucky."

"Somebody bet a bottle on it. That was a few days ago. There's rather more money involved now."

$HeOrShe gives the logs another look.

"I'm tired of hearing about it, and I'd rather they didn't start putting ship shares into the pot."

"Bring us $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk and we'll have something better than a sensor log to argue over."

"The pot is $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestReward. You've got $entity.catchreleaseFleetDays."

"Good. I'll send you the logs and the location."

The files arrive from $entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName.

"Bring us $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk and that should be the end of it."

"Fair enough."

The captain sends over the logs and the terms of the wager.

"If you happen across $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk in the next $entity.catchreleaseFleetDays, give us a hail."

"All right. I'll deal with them."

"$entity.catchreleaseFleetFlagshipName out."

"I stopped them taking any more bets until this is settled. That produced another argument, but at least nobody's putting up next month's pay."

"We still need $entity.catchrelease_fleetQuestAsk. $entity.catchreleaseFleetDays left."

A couple of crew from each watch come forward to inspect the catch. There is some muttering before the captain cuts them off and checks the specimens against the logs.

"That's enough. Pay out the bets."

The captain authorizes the transfer to your account.

"First watch saw the same kind of return several times and called it a run. Second watch says there wasn't enough there to call it anything."

The captain brings up the relevant entries.

"I've looked at both. I can see why they're arguing. I also don't intend to spend another shift doing it with them."

"That settles it. More or less."

The captain looks past the pickup toward someone off-screen.

"No, we're not taking bets on whether the catch was representative."

$HeOrShe looks back.

"Thanks, captain."

"Me? Neither."

The captain shrugs.

"If I knew which watch was right, we wouldn't need you."

text:
Your sensors officer picks a cold hull out of the debris field: an old auxiliary stripped farther than a salvage crew would ordinarily bother.

One object remains attached to the dorsal handling deck.

At first it reads as part of the ship. Closer inspection resolves a reinforced servicing frame with maneuvering thrusters, a dead transponder, and mounting points sized for something not much smaller than a fighter.

The frame is held to the wreck by three emergency clamps. None belong to the wreck.
options:

catchrelease_wreckTake:Recover the service assembly
catchrelease_wreckExplore:Explore the derelict
catchrelease_wreckLeave:Leave the wreck alone

text:
The boarding party finds an ordinary dead ship.

The reactor is cold. The lockers have been emptied. Someone took the expensive avionics and left the galley fittings. There are no bodies.

Your ops chief sends back imagery of the external frame.

"Different story out here. LYNE markings. Rig service codes, maybe. Half of them don't resolve against anything in the registry."

A closer image follows.

Someone has scratched maintenance intervals into the casing by hand.

Your crew can recover the assembly intact. It will take a cargo crane and several hours of unproductive swearing.

The transponder package still contains the last service handshake it accepted.

The source is listed simply as FISHERMAN.

The frame comes over on the heavy cargo crane.

It is larger aboard your ship than it looked outside: several tonnes of scarred mechanism, docking hardware, and sealed electronics wrapped around an empty space - clearly intended to hold a craft of some kind, now absent.

Your crew lash it down.

text:
Your comms officer catches a personal beacon running on emergency power.

The source is a prefabricated cache dug into the surface. Most of it is storage, but somebody has converted one compartment into living space.

The occupant is thin, dirty, and extremely pleased to see a ship.

A garbled transmission calls out almost immediately.

"You came back! Please take me aboard, $PlayerSirOrMadam, I beg of you!"

options: 30:catchrelease_ratingMuder:Order a cannon fired at the beacon

text:
"Missed the boat."

He sees your expression.

"Not like that. We were doing a transfer. Skipper thought I was aboard the tender. Tender thought I was aboard the ship. Everybody signed the same manifest and left."

He points to the beacon.

"By the time anyone worked it out, I wasn't on their route anymore. Probably thought I bailed on them."

text:
"Fishing crew."

He drinks from a dirty water pouch.

"Worked around the Fisherman's boats. If you're looking for them, go past the settled traffic and hail the trawlers."

He gives your comms officer the old fleet handshake.

"It still works."

You order bombardment of the coordinates the beacon is broadcasting from. 

It falls silent with a single shot.

He accepts before you finish the sentence.

Your personnel officer finds a spare berth.

The trawler answers without ceremony.

The Fisherman is at a worktable with a mug in one hand and a dismantled control unit under the other.

"Evening, captain. Buying, selling, or looking for work?"

"Back again."

The Fisherman shifts a service slate out of his working space.

"I've got range data if you're after something particular. Work if you're not."

A crewman crosses behind him carrying a sealed crate. Halfway across the compartment, his hands are empty.

The Fisherman's voice reaches the bridge a moment before the comm indicator turns green.

"Evening."

When the picture follows, he is pouring something into the same battered mug.

"What's the trouble?"

The link opens on the Fisherman watching somebody work off-screen.

"Easy with that."

A metallic impact follows from your left audio channel, though the trawler lies to starboard.

He looks back to you.

"Captain. What can I do for you?"

The Fisherman glances at the salvage manifest attached to your catch log.

"Bycatch."

He taps the entry once.

"Wreckage. Lost cargo, or a memory thereof. Whatever the retrieval rig brings up with the pattern."

He gives the manifest another look before continuing.

"The LYNE can only carry so much. If you want a chance at something bigger, you'll need a modified clamp. Ask around in bars. Somebody may have the schematics."

The hail is accepted promptly.

An older man in patched working clothes studies your transponder return. Grey beard, old scar tissue, the posture of someone who spent enough years on command decks to stop sitting properly in chairs.

"Haven't got you in the ledger."

He takes a drink.

"That's usually how new work starts."

The trawler cuts across your approach before you get much closer to the unstable fabric.

The Fisherman comes on the channel.

"Easy."

He looks at your ship, then toward the rupture.

"You've no ROD aboard. Another hundred klicks and I'll have to come fish you from the rupture instead of my catch."

He gestures away from it.

"Come alongside."

text:
The rating hears you out, then turns the glass between both hands.

"You're going beyond the picket?"

They nod vaguely upward.

"There's fishing work out there. Proper work, if you've got a ship and don't mind machinery that takes a crane to service. Look for a trawler holding outside the inhabited traffic lanes. Hail them."

A pause.

"Ask for the Fisherman."

"Ship's crew."

The rating lifts one shoulder.

"Not an officer. Deck, drives, guns, flight line, loading detail - whatever berth owns you that watch. Navy likes a proper word for everything."

They take a drink.

"Rating."

"That's what they call it."

The rating considers the objection.

"There's catch. There's buyers. There's gear. Sounds like fishing from my end of the loading bay."

"Past the last settled orbit. They don't berth much."

The rating gives you the relevant nav reference.

"If there's a boat in-system, your sensors will find it. If there isn't, go far enough out and there generally is."

script: CatchReleaseCMD addFisherQuestion catchrelease_ask_searchlightDrones "Why can't I use the drones with the searchlights?" false

text:
"The lights don't open a full breach. They wear the fabric thin enough for the ROD to reach through, but not enough for a drone to make the trip both ways."

He taps the harpoon schematic.

"Send a drone through one of those and it'll be stuck beyond the fabric. That's why the harpoon keeps the line back to the ship. The rig doesn't have to make the return crossing on its own."
"Good."

"Yes."

He considers that for a moment.

"There's a schematic for it. Rare one. Changes how the drone-side equipment handles a light-made breach."

"I've heard a rumor somebody has a copy."
"Do that."

text:
"Good. Work's the easy part to explain."

He calls up a handling manifest.

"Start with the rig."

"Fishing."

He lets the answer sit long enough to see whether it satisfies you.

It does not.

"Fair question. Easier to show you than talk around it."

"Fishing."

He lets the answer sit long enough to see whether it satisfies you.

It does not.

"Fair question. Easier to show you than talk around it."

He signals the deck crew.

"Come alongside."

"ROD device."

Your science officer quietly points out that the D already stands for Device.

The Fisherman hears this.

"Yes."

text:
"Depends which manual you found."

He reaches for a control slate.

"None of the good ones agree."

The Fisherman sends over a handling manifest.

Your ops chief reads the mass figure twice.

A cargo boom unfolds from the trawler and the LYNE drone comes across on external clamps. It is the size of a light fighter, built around a blunt ROD assembly and surrounded by maneuvering hardware. A launch rack follows, then the control package and enough supporting machinery to occupy a respectable section of working deck.

Nothing involved could reasonably be carried by a person.

"That's the line," the Fisherman says while your crew find somewhere to bolt it down. "One drone to start. Treat it well. Give the deck crew room for the launch, these run hot."

He sends your helm a local nav mark.

"Use it to break through the rupture nearby. Take one fish. Nothing ambitious. Bring it back and we'll go over the return."
options:
0:catchrelease_introRodOperate:Anything I should know before I use it?
10:catchrelease_introRodTrust:You give this equipment to every stranger who asks?

text:
"Point the fleet at some unstable fabric. Start the ROD to break it open, then let the drone work."

"Watch the return trace. If it starts getting ugly, stop and bring the drone home."

He closes the display.

"No."

He gives your fleet readout another look.

"I give it to captains I think will not squander it."

A small nod.

"Try not to make a liar of me."

The catch is transferred aboard the trawler.

The Fisherman checks the ROD telemetry first.

"Clean enough. Good."

Only then does he look at what you brought back.

"First trip's mostly about getting the rig home with you. You did."

text:
The corner of his mouth moves.

"Still got all the drones."

He nods.

"I'd call that a successful first trip."

"Pattern."

He turns the specimen container slightly.

"Fish is fine if you're buying supper. Pattern's the careful word."

The Fisherman brings up the deployment record.

"LYNE drones carry the ROD through the rupture. Drone goes through, gets a return, brings the pattern back across."

He zooms the display until the ROD trace fills it.

"Ghost is the old spacer word for what you're reaching after. Pattern is what the instruments can agree is there once the crossing gives it a shape."

He closes the plot.

"Usually looks like a fish."

"Don't know."

The Fisherman considers the specimen rather than the question.

"We tried asking it every way that seemed useful. None of the answers helped."

He closes the container record.

"Fish works well enough."

"Spacer word."

He shrugs.

"Good enough until somebody writes a better manual."

text:
The Fisherman puts the two retrieval logs side by side.

"There we are. Different pattern. Different kind of fabric."

A finger traces one coherence plot, then the other.

"That's enough to teach the instruments what you're looking at."

He closes both.

"You're ready for the outfitter."

A new service connection appears in your fleet systems.

A second transfer begins.

The first assembly is a bank of articulated projectors mounted on a reinforced frame. The second takes two cargo booms together: a harpoon launcher, ammunition handling gear, and a ROD head built into a projectile large enough to make the word harpoon seem modest.

The Fisherman watches your crew guide the first frame into place.

"Breach lights."

He points at the projector rig.

"Name's poor. They don't light much. They work the fabric until the ROD can punch through without a rupture."
"Outfitter's simple enough. Keep the drones flying, keep the return clean, fit the right core for the work. Mostly, it's a place to get better gear."

"Rig modules change how the gear works. Some more than others. All of them need a schematic."

"Swap it in when the work calls for it. No need to build the same module twice."

"Upgrade's a permanent improvement to the rig attributes."

He points out the tier listing.

"Buy the early tiers normally. The final two need a schematic each."

He holds a beaten slate up.

"Most people in the trade keep their own modifications on these. Do them a favor, they might part with a copy."

He taps the schematic.

"Bars are a good place to ask around. Working fleets, too."

"Probably wise."

He signals someone off-screen.

"Clear your heavy deck."

The Fisherman watches your crew guide the first frame into place.

"Breach lights."

He points at the projector rig.

He points at the second rig.

"That's a harpoon. Name's apt, this time."

"Quick and hard way to get a pattern. Lights thin the fabric enough to bring one within reach. Harpoon puts a ROD head on it before it slips away."

He looks directly at you.

"It's a heavy projectile. Treat it accordingly."

"They wear the fabric down until the ROD can reach through."

He closes it again.

"Run them away from people."
"The lights put out readings patrols don't care for. Use them well clear of planets and inhabited traffic."

He wipes a thumb across the display.

"Looks like rope. Isn't. Don't build procedures around the picture."

"It can put forty tonnes of bad judgment through a hull."

He considers the launcher.

"So can a cargo tug."

"Don't shoot either one at people."

text:
"Cut the lights."

$PersonRank $personName has your sensor signature on another display.

"Whatever rig you're running is throwing interference across $entity.catchrelease_lampWhere and the inhabited approaches around it."

"I'm warning you. Power it down."

"Hegemony Navy. Shut the device down."

$PersonRank $personName has your sensor return and the traffic plot side by side.

"Unlicensed high-energy operation inside a protected navigation volume. You have one warning."

"Kill the lights. Now."

"Corporate security."

A clean sensor plot appears beside $personName.

"Your equipment is producing effects outside your licensed operating envelope."

A polite smile.

"Power down."

"Extinguish it."

$PersonRank $personName looks past your bridge image toward the lamps.

"You were not given creation to cut at until something answers."

The traffic plot remains open.

"There are crews in those approaches, captain. Put the machine away from them."

The channel opens on a $manOrWoman already shouting.

"Kill it! Kill the lamp!"

$HeOrShe stabs a finger toward the sensor image.

"You wound God's work with Moloch's tools so you can drag supper through it, and you call that trade?"

Someone behind $himOrHer is shouting too.

"Extinguish it. Jettison it. Or we will do both for you."

"Kill the lights."

$personName points at a traffic plot.

"You are lighting up half our scopes and upsetting people who pay us specifically not to be upset."

"Do it somewhere emptier."

"By order of the Sindrian Diktat, cease operation."

$PersonRank $personName leaves the legal notice open between you.

"Whatever that apparatus is doing, it is doing it inside a volume under Sindrian authority."

The notice is tapped once.

"Shut it down before I am obliged to treat this as defiance."

"League patrol. Power it down."

$PersonRank $personName glances between your sensor return and a notice assembled from several local statutes.

"I can call this an unlicensed industrial operation and leave it there."

The notice is transmitted.

"That is the favourable interpretation. Use it."

"Hey. Lights off."

$personName looks at the sensor plot.

"I don't know what you've built. I know every instrument near $entity.catchrelease_lampWhere noticed it."

"Take it somewhere nobody lives."

"You've had the warning."

The previous incident sits open beside the new one.

"$entity.catchrelease_lampFineDGS credits. Pay it and shut the rig down."

"Second recorded operation."

"$entity.catchrelease_lampFineDGS credits."

"Pay. Power down. Leave."

"Repeat incident."

The settlement value appears.

"$entity.catchrelease_lampFineDGS."

"Further recurrence moves this out of billing."

"You were asked once."

The first warning remains open beside the new incident.

"A warning is mercy when it is heard. Ignored, it becomes indulgence."

"The fine is $entity.catchrelease_lampFineDGS credits."

"Pay it. Extinguish the lamps. Do not make another crew carry the cost of your choice."

"You kept it!"

The speaker is red-faced in the pickup.

"Of course you kept it. Moloch hands you a knife for creation and you haggle over the handle."

The figure flashes onto the channel.

"$entity.catchrelease_lampFineDGS credits. Pay it if numbers are the only language you still understand."

"Then kill the lamp. Next time we come aboard."

"Twice costs money."

"$entity.catchrelease_lampFineDGS."

"Next time costs ships."

"Second offense against a direct Sindrian order."

The penalty appears.

"$entity.catchrelease_lampFineDGS credits."

"You were told to cease operation. You chose to test whether the order was optional."

The figure remains on-screen.

"Pay it. Power down. Do not test the next one."

"Second recorded instance."

"$entity.catchrelease_lampFineDGS credits."

$PersonRank $personName closes the first notice and opens another.

"The third provision authorizes inspection and seizure. I'd rather not spend my afternoon invoking it."

"Pay the fine and shut the rig down."

"You again."

$personName puts the figure on-screen.

"$entity.catchrelease_lampFineDGS. Lights off."

"I'd like this to be the last time I learn something new about fishing."

"Cut the lamps and prepare for inspection."

$PersonRank $personName has stopped discussing the device.

"We are boarding for the equipment and anything recovered during the violation."

"Hegemony Navy. Heave to. Prepare to be boarded."

The officer does not read the warning history back to you.

"You ignored the warning and the fine. We are inspecting the rig and seizing recovery cargo covered by the incident."

"Cut the lights."

"Your operating privilege, insofar as one ever existed, is terminated."

The inspection order follows.

"Stand by for boarding. Recoveries associated with the incident are subject to seizure."

A final line appears beneath the order.

"Obstruction will be treated as a separate liability."

"Power it down."

The boarding order follows.

"You were warned, then fined. You have continued to put this work before the safety of every soul in those approaches."

The order is signed.

"We are coming aboard. What you brought back while using those lamps will not remain with you."

"Drives cold! Lamps cold!"

The speaker is close enough to the pickup for the image to shake with each word.

"We are coming aboard for what you dragged out under Moloch's light."

A weapon is shoved into view from somewhere behind $himOrHer.

"Touch a control and we'll count that as your answer."

"All right, captain. You've had the cheap versions."

A boarding shuttle separates from the formation.

"Lights off. Hold open."

The speaker looks past the camera.

"And don't make me put a price on resisting."

"Third offense against a direct order of the Sindrian Diktat."

The boarding authorization is signed.

"You have mistaken restraint for negotiability."

"Heave to. Your vessel will be inspected and the proceeds of the violation seized."

$PersonRank $personName opens the third provision.

"The convention has run out of prices. We are at remedies."

The boarding authorization follows.

"Inspection and seizure are authorized. Prepare to be boarded."

"I told you I didn't want to learn more about this."

A boarding authorization appears.

"Apparently I do."

"Pirates found our rupture. Now they collect protection on it."

The fisher turns the account sheet around.

"First payment bought us a week. Then they raised the rate because we kept working."

The slate marks $catchreleaseCampMany in the $catchreleaseCampWhere system.

"Get them off the rupture. Pay them, scare them, fight them, I don't care. Once they're gone, catch any fish from that exact rupture and bring it back. It has to be caught after we make the deal. Old cargo proves nothing."

"$catchreleaseDaysCap. Bring me $catchreleaseAsk from the cleared rupture and you get $catchreleaseRewardCap."

text:
The camp coordinates and pirate transponder codes are transferred.

"Whatever gets them off it. Just don't leave me owing them afterward."
The fisher closes the job entry and moves another maintenance payment into next month.

"Still there."

The fisher checks the camp marker.

"Raised the weekly number again, too."

"Camp's gone. Good."

$HeOrShe taps the rupture marker.

"Now bring me $catchreleaseAsk out of that spot. I need a catch from after it was cleared."

$HeOrShe checks the retrieval record, then deletes the protection payment from next month's accounts.

"Good. Boats go back out next shift."

The fisher accepts the call with both survey charts open and the claim file between them.

"Captain."

$HeOrShe closes a fresh message from the claims office without reading it twice.

"Any movement on your end?"

"A company survey moved the boundary."

The fisher overlays the charts.

"Their security contractor says the rupture falls inside the lease. My filed chart says it doesn't. The clerk won't decide while hired ships are sitting on the point."
